bullets.title: Oil surges to $90-98 on dual Red Sea chokepoint; macro regime shift underway
bullets.body: WTI crossed $90/bbl and Brent touched $98 following Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers and the U.S. conducting its 12th consecutive night of strikes on Iranian targets. Iran's IRGC warned shipping companies the southern Hormuz route is mined and threatened to halt all Gulf oil flow if attacked, while QatarEnergy prepared force-majeure LNG extensions through mid-October. GS base case is Brent $80/bbl 4Q26 but flags $120/bbl upside risk if disruptions persist; commodity prices since the Iran war began show sulfur +142%, European gas +97%, heating oil +62%.

bullets.title: Fed hike probability re-prices to ~30-33%; July hold expected but September live
bullets.body: Market-implied odds of a Fed rate hike by December 2026 reached 81% with two hikes priced by year-end, per Wolfe Research. July FOMC is expected to hold but multiple governors (Waller, Jefferson, Cook) are signaling willingness to tighten if core PCE stays above 0.25% MoM. The 2-year Treasury yield hit 4.31%, a 17-month high, and the 30-year yield is approaching its highest frequency of 5%+ closes since pre-GFC.

bullets.title: Yields surge globally: German 10Y at 3.20% (2011 high), Japan 2Y at 1.50% (30-year high)
bullets.body: German 10-year Bund yield reached 3.20%, its highest since 2011, and Japan's 2-year JGB climbed 6bp to 1.50%, the highest since May 1995. The yen weakened to a 40-year low against the dollar while Japan's Finance Minister flagged readiness for FX intervention. JGB futures fell in tandem with U.S. Treasuries, which sold off on Middle East escalation and inflation concerns.

bullets.title: GOOGL beats on Cloud (+82% YoY) but first-ever negative FCF and capex surge pressures stock
bullets.body: Alphabet Q2 revenue of $119.8B beat consensus by $2.7B; Google Cloud accelerated to +82% YoY with $514B backlog (+$52B Q/Q) and 35.6% margins. However, capex guidance was raised $15B to $195-205B for 2026 with further 'significant' increases in 2027 flagged (~$375-378B per MS/JPM models), driving Q2 FCF deeply negative for the first time in company history. Stock fell 3-5% AH; multiple sell-side firms cut PTs (JPM to $420, RJ to $400, Piper to $395) while Citi ($447) and Mizuho ($460) maintained buys.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex 'arms race' framing dominates sentiment; capex beneficiaries vs. hyperscalers is the key trade
bullets.body: GOOGL's capex reveal set the tone for MSFT/META/AMZN reporting next week. UBS noted hedge funds have been net shorting hyperscalers into earnings while being persistent buyers of AI Winners and US Semis. JPM's tactical view is long AI/Semis/Energy vs. short rates-sensitive; dealers are broadly short gamma in upside for META, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN making the pain trade higher. S&P 500 futures traded mixed (pre-market +0.6%) with KOSPI +3.7% on the GOOGL capex boost for the supply chain.

bullets.title: IMF/World Bank midyear: 3% global growth base case but 1.3% adverse; inflation raised to 4.7%
bullets.body: IMF raised 2026 headline inflation forecast to 4.7% from 4.1% citing energy price pressures. Global growth is projected at 3% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027 under a V-shaped recovery assumption that normalizes Hormuz by March 2027; adverse scenario with sustained energy disruption cuts growth to 1.3%. AI is seen offering 0.1%-0.8% medium-term productivity upside (World Bank sees up to 2.7% if transformative) but valuation concentration risk is flagged.

bullets.title: Fed forward guidance shifting; Warsh decentralizes communication away from Chair-centric model
bullets.body: Wolfe Research notes Chair Warsh has deliberately shifted market focus from Chair-centric speeches to broader FOMC member commentary, complicating signal interpretation. Policy statement next week will be minimal. Taylor Rule points to higher rates; option-implied probability of higher rates by December 2026 is 81%, with the base case being unchanged rates through year-end contingent on sub-0.25% MoM core PCE prints.

bullets.title: Software sector -15% YTD; IGV -11% YTD as AI disruption fears and PEGA miss weigh
bullets.body: IGV returned -11.1% YTD vs. S&P 500 +10.0% YTD. Wolfe's all-SaaS index trades at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales. PEGA's 16% decline after an AI-driven client delay miss and multiple downgrades reinforced enterprise AI adoption uncertainty. UBS noted HFs have been re-establishing US Software shorts since mid-July. PE firms are reportedly hunting 'SaaS-pocalypse' bargains in distressed software assets.

bullets.title: TXN beats and raises; industrial/auto cycle upturn broadening with data center doubling YoY
bullets.body: Texas Instruments reported Q2 revenue of $5.46B (+4% vs. consensus) and EPS of $2.14 (+11%), with Q3 guided to $5.90B midpoint (~7% above Street). Data Center revenue doubled YoY and is now ~12-13% of sales; automotive grew mid-teens YoY driven by China EV. Pricing increases are beginning to flow through with more impact expected in late 4Q26 and 2027. UBS raised PT to $380 citing 80%+ data center YoY growth and auto urgency.

bullets.title: INTC and AMD signing LTAs with Chinese data center customers; CPU prices in China up 40%+ YTD
bullets.body: Reuters reported Intel and AMD are pursuing multi-year server CPU supply agreements with major Chinese customers to lock in purchase volumes. Server CPU prices in China are up more than 40% YTD and still rising 10%+ month-on-month for some products. Intel is also seeking an operating partner for its delayed $28B Ohio fab, with SK Hynix among candidates. INTC +1% pre-market on the news.

bullets.title: AMD-Anthropic $5B strategic deal; 2GW MI450 deployment bullish for 2027-28 GPU revenue
bullets.body: AMD announced a strategic partnership with Anthropic involving up to 2GW of MI450 GPU deployment backed by a $5B AMD equity investment in Anthropic. UBS sees this as signaling conviction in upside to 2027 data center GPU revenue and a meaningful 2028 step-up. AMD's ROCm gap vs. CUDA is also expected to close faster as coding AI accelerates software development.

bullets.title: HF positioning: Mag-7 at 25th pct; semis rebuilt 30% of de-grossed positions; momentum stretched
bullets.body: Mag-7 hedge fund positioning is at the 25th percentile since January 2018 per JPM, making the pain trade higher. HFs have rebuilt ~30% of de-grossed semi positions and ~40% of memory exposure since last Friday but are still net short Hyperscalers into earnings. Separately, HF momentum positioning and gross leverage are near 5-year highs per other sources, flagging potential fragility.

bullets.title: DeepSeek/China AI: 12-18 month gap vs. US; Huawei chip access (~16K GPUs) and CUDA disruption
bullets.body: DeepSeek's Wenfeng reportedly believes the comprehensive China-US AI gap is 12-18 months and is working closely with Huawei, expecting to secure ~16,000 Huawei AI chips. AI-powered code generation and TileLang are expected to reduce CUDA dependency over time. The US is investigating Chinese AI firms' chip access after Moonshot AI allegedly distilled Anthropic's models; Treasury Secretary Bessent signaled potential entity list designations.

bullets.title: JPM quant: EPS revisions rising but prices lagging; rotate to quality/staples from tech/financials
bullets.body: Global 1-month EPS revisions hit +13.1% and 3-month +10.5%, but world markets are 2% below highs while semiconductors and momentum have sold off ~20%. JPM quant warns the two-year run of high-risk beating high-quality by +50% is reaching its limit and recommends rotating to Staples over Financials and Health Care over Technology. High EPS estimate dispersion stocks show signs of peaking.

bullets.title: US 2Q earnings tracking 37-40% YoY EPS growth; 80% beat rate with Big Tech leading at 81.7%
bullets.body: UBS reports 80% of S&P 500 companies have beaten estimates so far in 2Q with revenues tracking +12.6% YoY and EPS +37.3%. Big 6 Tech expected to deliver 81.7% YoY EPS growth vs. 23.7% for the rest of the market. Only Energy (+120.9%) and Tech+ (+81.4%) are expected to outpace the S&P 500 aggregate; EPS is on pace for 40.2% if historical revision trends hold. S&P 500 closed flat at 7,504.85 on Wednesday.

bullets.title: China and US working on tariff cut plan; MOFCOM reports close communication
bullets.body: China's Ministry of Commerce stated that China and the US are maintaining close communication and working on implementing a tariff reduction plan stemming from an earlier summit agreement. China is also seeking input on reciprocal US tariff cuts covering ~$30B in trade. This follows Intel and AMD's LTA moves with Chinese customers as the geopolitical landscape around tech exports remains fluid.

bullets.title: GE Vernova: 20 GW new gas contracts in Q2; capacity raised to 30 GW by 2030; stock oversold on 9% drop
bullets.body: GEV signed 20 GW of new gas contracts in Q2, beating 10-15 GW guidance, and increased turbine manufacturing capacity target to 30 GW by 2030 (from 24 GW). Data center orders hit $5B YTD (~2x FY25). Morgan Stanley raised PT to $1,350 calling the 9% stock decline an overreaction; GS BLUF and JPM both flag electricity investment cycle now in contracted, prepaid, multi-year commitments.

bullets.title: S&P 500 futures +0.6% pre-market at 7495; 10-year yield +4bp to 4.70%; WTI +4.5% to $90.72
bullets.body: Pre-market positioning shows S&P futures recovering modestly (+0.60% to 7494.75) driven by ServiceNow sympathy bid and GOOGL Cloud outperformance, offset by TSLA -7.3% and GOOGL -5.1% on capex concerns. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 4bp to 4.70% and WTI crude jumped 4.48% to $90.72 on geopolitical escalation. European futures were lower (DAX -0.53%, Euro Stoxx 50 -0.35%).
